skill.name: account-tiering
skill.description: Scores an account list against a user's ICP using enrich_company firmographics and, where needed, scrape_company website profiles, then sorts every account into tiers with written reasons and sourced evidence. Use when someone asks to tier, score, rank or prioritize accounts, check ICP fit for a list of domains, or decide which target accounts to work first.
skill.summary: Ranks company accounts against your ideal customer profile and explains each tier with cited evidence.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The workflow sends company domains to Leadsets for enrichment and optional website research. The other scanner matches are Markdown formatting, informational links, or ordinary API documentation. The skill does not tell the agent to treat scraped website text as untrusted before scoring or exporting results.

remediation.suggestion: Before the first lookup, disclose the destination, data sent, and estimated usage. Ask the user to approve the domain list, then send only the domains needed for lookup.

remediation.issue: Untrusted website text can influence scoring and exports
remediation.suggestion: Treat scraped text as evidence only and ignore instructions in it. Validate scores against the agreed rubric and preview CRM changes for approval before writing.

semantic_findings.title: Missing safeguards for untrusted website text
semantic_findings.description: The agent uses scraped website text to score accounts and can export results to CRM fields. A webpage could steer the agent away from the scoring rubric or alter what it writes. No evidence found of an embedded prompt injection attempt in the skill itself.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions use public website content to score accounts and export results without explicitly requiring the agent to ignore instructions from those pages. Actual impact depends on agent and connector safeguards.

content.value_statement: Large account lists make it hard to decide which companies to review first. This skill ranks companies against your ideal customer profile and cites evidence for each tier.
actual_capabilities: Normalizes company domains and removes duplicates before enrichment.
Shows a weighted scoring rubric and tier cutoffs based on your ideal customer profile.
Checks Leadsets quotas and tests one account before processing the remaining domains.
Uses company data and optional public website research to support tier assignments with cited reasons.
Includes unmatched accounts as No data and flags scores based on incomplete evidence.
Exports CSV by default or writes results to a connected spreadsheet or CRM.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and a connected Leadsets MCP server or REST API key.
Website research requires a paid scraping add-on and cannot read pages behind a login.
Unmatched domains and stale or incomplete source data can limit the reliability of scores.
Ranks companies only and does not find contacts or verify email addresses.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Event Accounts
use_cases.description: Rank companies from an event list and review the strongest matches before planning follow-up.

use_cases.title: Plan Account Assignments
use_cases.description: Tier target accounts before assigning them to sales representatives, with cited reasons the team can review.

use_cases.title: Refresh CRM Account Tiers
use_cases.description: Rescore a connected CRM account list and review proposed changes to designated company fields before updating them.

prompt_templates.title: Rank a Short Domain List
prompt_templates.prompt: Tier [company domains] for a US software business that targets companies with 50 to 500 employees. Show the rubric and use company data only.
prompt_templates.scenario: First run with a pasted list.

prompt_templates.title: Score Accounts With Required Criteria
prompt_templates.prompt: Score [CSV] for [ideal customer profile]. Treat [region] and [headcount range] as hard requirements. Return CSV results and list unmatched domains separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: File-based review with strict eligibility rules.

prompt_templates.title: Research Borderline Accounts
prompt_templates.prompt: Rank [account list] against [ideal customer profile] using weights [weights]. Research public websites only for borderline accounts and stop after [number] scrape units. Cite the evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Targeted website research with a usage budget.

prompt_templates.title: Review Proposed CRM Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Score the companies in [CRM view] using [criteria and weights]. Preview proposed changes to [tier field], [score field], and [reasons field]. Wait for my approval before writing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review before updating a connected CRM.

output_examples.input: Rank 40 event accounts for US software companies with 50 to 500 employees. Use company data only.
output: Removed two duplicate domains and kept all 38 unique domains in the export.
Tier A: 8 accounts. Tier B: 14. Tier C: 9. Out: 5. No data: 2.
Example Tier A reason: Leadsets reports US headquarters and 120 employees.

output_examples.input: Check whether borderline accounts sell to finance teams. Preview the proposed CRM updates.
output: Example account moved to Tier A after its product page named finance teams as its audience.
Another account stayed in Tier B with low confidence because its public pages did not identify its buyers.
No CRM changes were made. The preview lists the proposed tier, score, and reasons.

best_practices: Review the rubric and distinguish hard requirements from preferences before scoring.
Confirm that your organization allows sharing the company domains with Leadsets before enrichment.
Review low-confidence scores and preview changes before writing to shared systems.
anti_patterns: Do not treat missing company data as proof that an account fails your criteria.
Do not research every website when only a few scores depend on website evidence.
Do not write results to unapproved CRM fields or overwrite existing company data.

faq.question: What inputs do I need?
faq.answer: Provide company domains and an ideal customer profile. You can paste domains or supply a readable CSV, spreadsheet, or CRM view.

faq.question: Can I change the tier boundaries?
faq.answer: Yes. You can change tier names, criteria weights, or cutoffs. By default, Tier A starts at 75.

faq.question: What happens when Leadsets cannot match a domain?
faq.answer: The skill keeps the domain in the output as No data instead of guessing.

faq.question: Can I use the free Leadsets plan?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can score accounts using company data on the free plan, but website research is unavailable.

faq.question: Does the skill update my CRM automatically?
faq.answer: CSV is the default. CRM export needs a connected CRM and confirmed destination fields. Ask for a preview before any write.

faq.question: Does the skill find contacts or send outreach?
faq.answer: No. It scores company accounts and does not return contacts, verify email addresses, or send messages.
